items.title: Aethon: A Reference-Based Replication Primitive for Constant-Time Instantiation of Stateful AI Agents
items.body_heading: 从完整物化到分层实例化

exact_v1_locators.mechanism: exact-v1 HTML §4 System Architecture, paragraphs S4.p1-S4.p8; §5 Memory Model, paragraphs S5.p6-S5.p13

checks.mechanism_accuracy: passed — definition/reference/resolution substrates, layered inheritance, copy-on-write overlays and execution-time resolution match exact-v1
checks.old_path_rationale: passed — full materialization is retained for small state, low instance count, stronger isolation and simpler debugging
checks.changed_constraint: passed — repeated stable state and shared ancestry create startup, memory and lineage pressure at high instance counts
checks.state_data_control_ownership: passed — platform owns versioned definitions, lineage, resolution policy and lifecycle management; AgentRun owns local divergence; tools/environments retain side-effect authority
checks.gain_and_cost: passed — avoids eager stable-state copying while moving work and operational risk into resolution, caching, invalidation and overlay lifecycle
checks.failure_fallback_coexistence: passed — nondeterministic or expensive resolution, stale inheritance and unbounded overlay graphs are explicit; complete materialization remains the fallback/coexisting path
checks.evidence_boundary: passed — the body and Review note identify a conceptual reference design and explicitly reject empirical constant-time, memory, determinism, multitenancy and production-superiority claims
checks.owner_and_chapter_coherence: passed — the delta extends version-pinned Agent Definition/AgentRun identity and hands off naturally to the following typed Session branch/merge discussion
checks.placement: passed — mechanism body and marker are before Review notes; no mechanism body for this family appears after Review notes
checks.non_list_prose: passed — integrated as an old-boundary-to-mechanism-to-trade-off reasoning chain, not a paper list

items.adversarial_boundary_note: The exact-v1 treats resolver determinism, caching/invalidation and garbage collection as implementation obligations/open work. The Books text likewise assigns these to the platform as required responsibilities and does not claim that Aethon implemented or validated them.
